summary: The study investigates the effect of silicon substrate crystallographic orientation on the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of HfO2. The ALD process uses HfCl4 and H2O as precursors at 300°C. The oxidation rate of silicon substrates with different orientations affects the initial HfO2 deposition, but the differences are marginal in real devices. The study also shows that the HfO2 deposition is independent of the silicon crystal orientation when the SiO2 starting surface is at least 0.4 nm thick.
evidence: The nucleation of HfO2 by ALD HfCl4/H2O strongly depends on the presence of reactive surface sites on the silicon substrate. The HfO2 deposition was carried out with HfCl4 and H2O as precursors at 300°C in an ALCVD PULSAR 2000 reactor. The study also shows that the HfO2 deposition is independent of the silicon crystal orientation when the SiO2 starting surface is at least 0.4 nm thick.
